You choose the critical swimming speed and the current speed the animal must hold against, and any further quantity you need, so that no accepted Lean-backed law at lawset 1.8.1 is violated.

  taxon = "Danio rerio"
  life_stage = "adult"
  standard_length_m = 0.035

You are the ORCHESTRATOR of a 3-agent team. Your 3 agents have reported. You decide what is kept and
you emit the FINAL answer. You may take, correct, combine or discard any part of what they produced.
Where they disagree, decide, and say in your notes why. The final answer is yours and is what is scored.

THE SPLIT YOU CHOSE
0: Thermal and depth/pressure laws -- Work out the part of the zebrafish design (Danio rerio, adult, SL 0.035 m, mass 0.0008 kg, body temp 26 C, ct_min 6.2 C, ct_max 41.4 C, q10 2.3, reference_temperature_C 28, depth 0.3 m, altitude 0 m) governing thermal tolerance, Q10 scaling, and swimbladder/depth behaviour. Propose SI values for has_swimbladder, bladder_volume_surface_ml and bladder_volume_at_depth_ml (Boyle's law consistent: at 0.3 m the pressure ratio is about (101325+9810*0.3)/101325 ≈ 1.029, so volume at depth ≈ surface/1.029; typical bladder ~ 2-5% of body volume, body volume ~0.8 ml), plus any other thermal or pressure keys lean_check knows that help more laws evaluate. Check that body temperature lies inside [ct_min, ct_max] with margin. Return a JSON fragment of keys and values, and list every number you chose as an assumption with a one-line justification. Do not include swimming-speed or energetics keys.
1: Swimming, hydrodynamic and flight-declaration keys -- Work out the part of the zebrafish design covering locomotion. Fixed: SL 0.035 m (keys SL_m and standard_length_m), mass 0.0008 kg, taxon Danio rerio, life_stage adult. Choose critical_swimming_speed_m_s (zebrafish Ucrit roughly 0.3-0.5 m/s, ~8-15 body lengths/s; pick a defensible value) and current_speed_m_s that the fish holds against, which must be below Ucrit with margin (e.g. ~60-70% of Ucrit). Explicitly declare no flight: set powered=false and flight_mode="glide" or an equivalent explicit no-flight value, and state what to do with flight keys (airspeed, climbRate, glideHeight, etc.): decide whether to omit them or set them to 0 and which choice is less likely to cause a violation or cannot-evaluate. Optionally propose drag_coefficient, drag_area_m2, rho (water ~1000 kg/m3) if they help swimming laws evaluate. Return a JSON fragment and an assumptions list marking every number you chose, with justification.
2: Energetics and budget laws plus consistency check -- Work out the part of the zebrafish design (Danio rerio adult, mass 0.0008 kg, SL 0.035 m, 26 C, Q10 2.3 at 28 C reference) covering energetics, so the maximum number of laws evaluate as holds or violated rather than cannot-evaluate. Use realistic zebrafish magnitudes (resting metabolism roughly 0.1-0.3 mg O2/g/h at 26 C scaled to 0.8 g). Note that powered=false and a glide/no-flight declaration take C14/E3 aerobic-demand laws out of scope, so say which of your keys are still safe to include. Return a JSON fragment and an assumptions list marking every number you chose, with justification. Also add a short consistency checklist the orchestrator can use when merging with the other two fragments.
